title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
abstract: arXiv:2611.17440v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. We find that agents with similar solve rates can nevertheless differ substantially in how they explore, modify and verify code. translated_title: 通过行为轨迹解读编码智能体
translated_abstract: 标准的编码智能体基准测试主要评估二元化的任务成功与否，将执行过程视为黑箱，掩盖了产生这些结果的行为。我们分析了来自125种智能体配置、涵盖117个不同模型的大型语料库，共143,209条执行轨迹。为了能在异构的智能体接口之间进行比较，我们开发了一个基于规则的解析器，将原始执行痕迹映射为仓库搜索、文件编辑、测试执行等高级动作，并针对500个事件以六模型共识参考对其预测进行了审计。我们发现，解决率相近的智能体在探索、修改和验证代码的方式上仍可能存在显著差异。此外，在不使用任务结果、token数量或工具名称作为特征的情况下，汇总的行为画像能够在不相交的仓库集合和不同编程语言中检索出对应的智能体技术栈，尽管任务构成尚未被完全……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种基于规则的解析器，将编码智能体的原始执行轨迹映射为高级行为，并通过对14万余条轨迹的行为画像分析，揭示解决率相近的智能体在探索、修改和验证代码的方式上存在显著差异，且这些行为画像本身足以在不同仓库与语言间识别出对应的智能体技术栈。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a rule-based parser that maps coding agents' raw execution traces into high-level behaviors, and using behavioral profiles from over 143K trajectories shows that agents with similar solve rates differ substantially in how they explore, modify, and verify code, while behavioral profiles alone can identify the underlying agent stack across disjoint repositories and programming languages.
